Wait out usage limits on a pane, unattended

Usage:
  cmux watch

Watches a pane and, when Claude Code's usage-limit menu appears, chooses the
option that waits — preferring one that then continues automatically, so the
session resumes without a human.

It never presses Upgrade your plan or Add funds. If the menu is not one cmux
recognises, it says so and presses nothing: a wrong press here costs money.

Prefer cmux rate-limit-options. Arming that ahead of time means the menu never
blocks in the first place; watch is the net for when it was not armed.

This is the only cmux command that keeps running. It reads the menu off the
screen, so a change to how Claude Code draws it will break watch — the
wording it looks for is one list in internal/menu/limit.go.

Example:
  cmux --to %12 watch --interval 10s

Flags for watch:
  --interval <duration>  how often to look at the pane (default 15s)
  --once                 stop after the first time the menu is dealt with

Flags:
  --to <target>      pane id (%12), session:window.pane, or an index from cmux panes
  --all-panes        allow a target that was not detected as Claude Code
  --dry-run          print the tmux calls instead of making them
  --defer <seconds>  have tmux deliver the keys later, via run-shell
  --self             allow interrupt to target the pane cmux was run from
  -h, --help         show help
  --version          show version
